benchmark_method: Five sequential runs per binary per workload, alternating order; normal clocks; posix_spawn and per-child wait4; warm filesystem caches, no explicit warmup; raw outputs compared on every pair.
phase: Sixth pass: frequency burden, Mendel, discordance, allele counts, FORMAT encoding and PCA/DGEEV
baseline_scope: CLI regression against original commit in matching configurations; incremental performance against frozen fifth-pass source and binaries. Perl source unchanged this pass.

normal.clock: fixed_time.c linked in both executables; no output normalization

lapack.clock: fixed_time.c linked in both executables; no output normalization

format_probe.scope: Actual linked parse_FORMAT and print_bcf, exhaustive small token patterns plus duplicate/unknown/reordered tags, mixed numeric widths and long fields. Raw FORMAT bytes and compressed BGZF records are compared.
limitations: Not a whole CLI test; records.bgzf contains encoded records without a BCF file header.
Overfull sample fields are excluded: original format_matrix indexes past its row size.
Unknown middle/first fields exercise parse_FORMAT only because print_bcf has separate legacy indexing assumptions.

When --fallback-threshold is given, only that constant is lowered in a separate compiled source copy; this exercises the production fallback body without allocating a 2-GiB string. It does not execute the actual INT_MAX-sized input.
Explicit object directories must match the supplied headers.

format_fallback_probe.scope: Actual linked parse_FORMAT and print_bcf, exhaustive small token patterns plus duplicate/unknown/reordered tags, mixed numeric widths and long fields. Raw FORMAT bytes and compressed BGZF records are compared.
limitations: Not a whole CLI test; records.bgzf contains encoded records without a BCF file header.
Overfull sample fields are excluded: original format_matrix indexes past its row size.
Unknown middle/first fields exercise parse_FORMAT only because print_bcf has separate legacy indexing assumptions.

When --fallback-threshold is given, only that constant is lowered in a separate compiled source copy; this exercises the production fallback body without allocating a 2-GiB string. It does not execute the actual INT_MAX-sized input.
Explicit object directories must match the supplied headers.

dgeev_probe.contract: Bit-exact Er, Ei and eigenvector matrices; same linked LAPACK and source sort definitions.
limitations: Finite matrix inputs to LAPACK only; malformed dimensions and arbitrary LAPACK failures excluded.
Sorting fixtures include quiet NaN payloads, but signaling-NaN traps are not modeled.

burden_mendel_model.scope: Independent algorithm models; real command output must also be compared. Memory bound counts int payload and pointer slots, not allocator overhead/RSS. No existing int block is copied or replaced during accumulation. Signed int counter-overflow behavior is unchanged and not modeled.

scratch_comparison.method: Complete raw-byte multisets; random private filenames ignored only. Public outputs and diagnostics remain byte-exact.

workloads.name: burden-all-blocks-1000
workloads.description: Every sample touches every 256-bin block through rotated carrier windows; all rows allocate the full logical width. Dense allocation control without prefix-only row coverage.

workloads.name: burden-empty-2000
workloads.description: 2000 samples / no records; all output bins remain present but require no counters.

workloads.name: burden-full-frequency-control
workloads.description: 1000 samples, every allele-count bin1..2000 visited in increasing order; forces dense rows and repeated growth.

workloads.name: burden-rare-2000
workloads.description: 2000 samples / 2000 singleton sites; every sample touched, only bin1 needed; full zero output retained.

workloads.name: burden-rare-carriers-2000
workloads.description: 2000 samples / 2000 singleton sites; every sample touched, only bin1 needed; full zero output retained.

workloads.name: burden-tail-block-512
workloads.description: Every sample touches every 256-bin block through rotated carrier windows; all rows allocate the full logical width. Final block holds exactly one counter.

workloads.name: diff-counts-many-samples
workloads.description: 32768 samples / 6 shared sites; missing halves and discordant calls.

workloads.name: diff-counts-many-sites
workloads.description: 2048 samples / 1200 shared sites; missing halves and discordant calls.

workloads.name: encoding-many-long-fields
workloads.description: 512 samples, four 4-KiB string FORMAT fields, three records; isolates removal of the N-by-F string matrix.

workloads.name: encoding-many-short-fields
workloads.description: 4096 samples, short string FORMAT columns, forty records; allocation/throughput control.

workloads.name: encoding-single-long-field
workloads.description: 512 samples, one 16-KiB string FORMAT field, three records; isolates whole-binary-copy removal.

workloads.name: mendel-heterozygous
workloads.description: 100 trios / 4000 sites; four unique parental products and occasional errors with nonempty output.

workloads.name: mendel-homozygous-control
workloads.description: 100 trios / 4000 sites; old set deduplicates to one product, with occasional nonempty errors.

workloads.name: pca-512x1025
workloads.description: Complete polymorphic diploid sites; ordinary PCA retains no M after unchanged Gram construction.

workloads.name: pca-512x2048-no-normalisation
workloads.description: Complete polymorphic diploid sites; ordinary PCA retains no M after unchanged Gram construction.

workloads.name: pca-small-control
workloads.description: Complete polymorphic diploid sites; ordinary PCA retains no M after unchanged Gram construction.

sort_workloads.scope: Actual sorting functions; includes process startup, deterministic matrix initialization and complete binary output. Not an end-to-end PCA speed claim.

rejected_contiguous_growth.decision: Replaced reallocating contiguous rows with fixed 256-counter blocks after dense RSS regression; allocator-retained freed row capacities outweighed sparse gains.

model.scope: Independent algorithm models; real command output must also be compared. Memory bound counts int payload slots, not allocator overhead/RSS. Signed int counter-overflow behavior is unchanged and not modeled.

limitations: Finite same-platform tests and defined baseline behavior only; not a universal proof for every input, toolchain, architecture or resource-exhaustion path.
Fixed clocks control CLI diagnostics/RNG without output normalization. Normal-clock benchmark elapsed-time diagnostics are retained separately; raw result files, stdout and exits match.

Frequency-burden zeros, bin width, integer increment order and legacy masked sample labels remain unchanged. Dense blocks store the same exact int payload plus pointer directories and allocator overhead; sparse RAM savings do not guarantee dense nonincrease.
Original N*2/count overflow and invalid positive genotype indexing remain outside defined compatibility. Lazy allocation can change resource-exhaustion failure timing.

FORMAT token cursors preserve legacy short-row inheritance, empty fields, unknown/duplicate tag behavior. Very long strings use the old splitter; fallback body is separately tested with a lowered threshold, not a real greater-than-2-GiB input.

Original overfull FORMAT token rows have out-of-bounds accesses; unknown leading/middle fields probe parse_FORMAT but exclude legacy unsafe print_bcf indexing. No compression parameters changed; tests include compressed bytes.

Eigen sort keeps quiet NaNs as barriers and preserves tie/signed-zero/payload bytes. Signaling-NaN traps and malformed LAPACK dimensions/failures are not modeled. Same Accelerate library and thread limit used.
Ordinary PCA releases M only after the unchanged Gram computation; SNP-loadings M remains live. Original ragged M rows for negative genotype sums remain a separate undefined-behavior issue.
Removed unused LAPACK arrays reduce requested allocation, but uncommitted pages need not lower peak RSS. Sort adds an int permutation and logarithmic stack; actual RAM increases are recorded.
All Perl source matches fifth pass; historical Perl nondeterminism/tabix limitations remain applicable and historical pass counts are not added to this pass.
